options.description: Match normalized paths preserving the command-line root spelling, so discovered files appear as `src/gen/about.py`; accept both slash styles through the existing regex transformation.
options.label: CLI-relative path

options.description: Match every discovered path relative to the current working directory, even when the supplied target is absolute or uses a different spelling.
options.label: Working-directory relative

options.description: Match canonical absolute paths, requiring anchored patterns to include the full filesystem prefix.

question.prompt: For `pylint --recursive=y src/` with `ignore-paths = ["^src/gen/.*$"]`, which path representation should `ignore-paths` match?

options.description: Normalize only paths produced by `_discover_files`, leaving other ignore-path matching behavior unchanged.

open_material_decisions: Define how anchored project-relative ignore-path patterns behave when the recursive command-line target is absolute.

options.description: Normalize separators but preserve whether the command-line target was relative or absolute; anchored project-relative patterns require a relative target.

acceptance_checks: Add a regression test for recursive discovery from a relative target spelled with a trailing separator and `ignore-paths = ^src/gen/.*$`; verify generated Python files are absent while a nonignored file remains.
Cover Windows-style discovered candidates and verify they match the anchored Posix-style pattern after separator-only normalization.
Verify the equivalent anchored Windows-form configuration remains supported through the existing path-regex transformation.
Verify an anchored project-relative pattern does not match when recursive discovery is invoked with an absolute target.
Verify separator normalization is exercised consistently in recursive directory checks, top-level `expand_modules` filtering, and package/namespace submodule filtering.
Verify basename-based `ignore` and `ignore-patterns` behavior is unchanged.
Run the targeted lint/config/module-expansion tests and the relevant recursive self-test suite.
confirmed_decisions: `ignore-paths` evaluates the path representation derived from the command-line target, so a relative target such as `src/` produces match candidates such as `src/gen/about.py`.
Candidate path normalization converts backslashes to forward slashes only.
Normalization preserves relative versus absolute form, including the user's target spelling; absolute targets are not converted to project-relative paths.
No lexical cleanup or canonicalization is performed: dot segments, redundant components, symlinks, and case remain unchanged.
The normalization applies to every ignore-path check, including recursive discovery, top-level expansion, and package or namespace submodule checks.
`ignore` and `ignore-patterns` continue matching basenames under their existing behavior.
Existing support for configuring ignore-path regexes in Posix or Windows form must remain compatible.
contract.summary: Fix `ignore-paths` matching by normalizing only candidate path separators to `/` immediately before every ignore-path regex evaluation. Preserve the candidate's command-line-derived spelling and whether it is relative or absolute; do not resolve, absolutize, relativize, case-fold, collapse dot segments, or resolve symlinks. Apply this consistently to recursive directory discovery, top-level module expansion, and package/namespace submodule filtering. Thus `pylint --recursive=y src/` with `^src/gen/.*$` excludes files such as `src\gen\about.py` on Windows, while the same pattern does not match files discovered from an absolute target such as `C:\project\src`. Existing basename-based `ignore` and `ignore-patterns` semantics remain unchanged.

interviewer.reason: The requested behavior and success criteria are sufficiently clarified. The implementation must make ignore-path matching separator-independent while preserving the command-line-derived path spelling and relative/absolute form.
